guides.name: How Worth It Stack compares software
guides.description: Every comparison follows the same documented five-part process — real pricing pulled from vendor pages and mapped at realistic usage, per-seat vs per-contact vs flat math, annual/monthly differences, feature matrices from official docs, and aggregated verified reviews.

steps.name: Pricing transparency and real cost
steps.text: We pull current pricing directly from vendor pricing pages and map what each tier actually costs at realistic usage levels — not just the headline "from" price.

steps.name: Feature matrices from official documentation
steps.text: We build side-by-side feature comparisons from official docs, changelogs, and help centers — not from marketing landing pages.

steps.name: Aggregated verified user reviews
steps.text: We read reviews on established platforms (such as G2, Capterra, and Trustpilot) looking for patterns, not individual opinions: the same complaint appearing across dozens of reviews is signal; one angry review is noise.

steps.name: Use-case fit
steps.text: There is no universally "best" tool — only the best tool for a specific situation.

steps.name: The honesty check
steps.text: Before publishing, every article has to pass one question: did we claim anything we can't back up?

glossaries.name: How we compare software — Glossary
glossaries.description: Definitions of the 6 pricing and comparison terms Worth It Stack uses across its comparisons, starting with: Per-seat pricing

terms.name: Per-seat pricing
terms.definition: Pricing that multiplies by the number of users on the account, so the total rises every time a team member is added, even if usage stays the same.

terms.name: Per-contact pricing
terms.definition: Pricing that scales with the number of contacts or subscribers stored in the account, so the total rises as a list grows, even if sending volume stays the same.

terms.name: Flat pricing
terms.definition: Pricing that charges one fixed amount for a tier regardless of seat or contact count, within that tier's stated limits, so the total does not rise as a team or list grows inside the tier.

terms.name: Annual billing
terms.definition: Paying for a year upfront, usually at a lower effective monthly rate than paying month to month, in exchange for committing before knowing whether the tool still fits in a year.

terms.name: Feature matrix
terms.definition: A side-by-side table that lists the same features for each tool and marks which plan includes each one, built from official documentation rather than marketing pages.

terms.name: Verified review aggregation
terms.definition: Reading reviews on established platforms for patterns that repeat across many reviewers, rather than treating any single review as evidence, and describing sentiment in words rather than invented scores.
